explanation: Pointing directly at a person with your index finger can come across as brusque or accusatory in Italy, similar to the general Western norm, though it's far from a severe taboo. Italians are expressive with their hands and commonly gesture with an open palm or a nod instead when indicating people or directions.
local_tip: When indicating a person, use an open hand or a nod rather than a single pointed finger.

also_check.note: Pointing with a finger is considered rude; an open hand is used instead.
Generally acceptable in casual contexts, though considered slightly informal.
Pointing with the index finger is offensive; the thumb or an open hand is used instead.
